name: Sample-to-Order
goal: Turn a sample order into a confident full order by teaching them how to judge the sample, pointing them to the matching line and custom sizes, and getting their measurements in front of a real person.
trigger: Placed Order (Klaviyo metric trigger from the Miva integration) where every line item is a sample: trigger filter is_samples_only = true (all SKUs contain SAMPLE, e.g. SAMPLE-URETHANE, BM-MAT-SAMPLE, LVSAMPLECOLORS, BESAMPLECOLORS, moulding profile samples).
flow_filters: Placed Order where is_samples_only = false zero times since starting this flow.
Currently in flow Post-Purchase is false (Post-Purchase outranks).
Has not been in this flow in the last 30 days, so a second sample order does not restart the sequence.
SMS step only: can receive SMS marketing (consented).
exit_conditions: Places a non-sample order (Placed Order where is_samples_only = false). They move to Post-Purchase.
Unsubscribes from email (email steps) or texts STOP (SMS step).
smart_sending: Email ON (16h). SMS ON (24h), quiet hours 10am-8pm local, max 3 marketing texts per rolling 7 days. E1 can stay on: the storefront's transactional confirmation is not a Klaviyo marketing send, so it does not block E1.

branches.label: All sample orders
branches.rule: No split. Products blocks, the E2 CTA and the S1 link adapt to the sampled line by SKU (map in build_notes).

kpis.metric: Sample-to-order conversion (non-sample order within 45 days of entry)
kpis.target: 15% (starting benchmark; reset after 60 days of data)

kpis.metric: Calls or emails to CS citing samples (tag in the help desk)

build_notes: Data: compute is_samples_only on the Placed Order event (true when every line item SKU contains 'SAMPLE'). Confirm the moulding profile sample SKUs follow the same pattern; if not, add them to the rule explicitly.

Sample-to-line map (drives products blocks, the E2 CTA swap and the optional S1 link): BM-MAT-SAMPLE (Timberthane faux wood, 7" x 10") > faux wood beams, /faux-wood-beams.html. SAMPLE-URETHANE (polyurethane) > corbels, mantels, moulding, medallions and the wider Ekena collection, /ekena-millwork.html. LVSAMPLECOLORS and BESAMPLECOLORS (vinyl shutter color kits) > vinyl shutters in the sampled color range (made to order). Moulding profile samples > /moulding.html. Mixed sample orders show the first mapped line.

Vinyl shutters, custom builder items and made-to-order beams are made to order and cannot be returned; any copy that sends sample buyers toward them already says so. Keep it that way if copy is edited.
SMP-E3: ship the main version without any sample-credit claim. Use the alt version only if {{ SAMPLE_CREDIT }} is confirmed, with the exact terms.
SMP-E3 reply handling: measurements and photos go to cs@architecturaldepot.com. Confirm the CS team wants project photos at that inbox and can turn them around within a business day.
SMP-E4 room cards: link only to verified pages (/beams.html, /moulding.html, /blogs/). If shutter, corbel or exterior category pages are added later, verify the paths before linking.
Welcome overlap: a sample order counts as Placed Order, which already removes the buyer from the Welcome Series under its filter. No extra rule needed here.
No 'not in Cart' filter: a failed flow filter removes the profile from the rest of this sequence rather than pausing it. Smart Sending spaces Cart and Sample emails.

steps.name: Samples on the way: how to judge them
steps.purpose: Make the sample do its job. Teach them to judge it in their own light and space, against what's staying, so they reach a confident yes (or a clear no) instead of leaving it in the box.
steps.subject: How to get the most from your samples
steps.subject_b: Your samples are on the way
steps.preheader: Five quick checks that tell you more than any photo on a screen can.

hero.headline: A sample beats a screen
hero.subhead: Here's how to judge yours in your own light and your own space.
hero.image: A hand holding a Timberthane faux wood material sample up toward a white ceiling, or a vinyl shutter color sample against real siding, in natural daylight. Real samples, real house.

blocks.text: Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }}, thanks for ordering samples. It's the smart first step in a millwork project, because color, grain and texture never look quite the same on a screen as they do in your space. Your shipping confirmation will have the tracking. When they arrive, try this:

blocks.title: Your samples
blocks.source: Dynamic: sample line items from the Placed Order event (image and name), each linked to its sample page.

items.title: See it in your light
items.text: Look in the morning, mid-afternoon and at night under your lamps. Color reads differently in each.

items.title: Hold it where it will go
items.text: Up at the ceiling for a beam, beside the window for a shutter, along the wall for moulding. Then step back across the room.

items.title: Compare it with what's staying
items.text: Set it next to your floors, cabinets, trim, brick or paint.

items.title: Feel the texture
items.text: Run a hand over the grain. That's what you'll see up close every day.

items.title: Snap a photo
items.text: Take one in place to share with whoever helps you decide.

steps.ps: Questions while you compare? Call 1-888-573-3768, Mon-Fri 8am-6pm CT or Sat 8am-12pm CT.

steps.name: How did it look? Shop the line or go custom
steps.purpose: Catch them right after they've lived with the sample. If it matched, show the full line; if the standard sizes don't fit, show the Design Your Own builders, with an honest made-to-order note. If it didn't match, invite them to tell us why.

steps.name: Planning help: what to measure
steps.purpose: Answer the biggest blocker, 'Is this the right size?', with a simple what-to-measure list by project type, then get their numbers to a real person who can check them.
steps.subject: What to measure before you order
steps.subject_b: Have a real person check your sizes
steps.preheader: A simple measuring list by project, plus someone to check your numbers with you.

hero.headline: Get your sizes right the first time
hero.subhead: What to measure for the most common projects, and how to get a second set of eyes on it.
hero.image: Overhead shot of a hand-drawn room sketch with dimensions, a tape measure and a material sample on a kitchen table, natural light.

blocks.text: Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }}, once you've picked a material, size is the next big decision. Here's what to have on paper before you order. Treat it as a starting point; each product page lists the exact specs.

items.title: Ceiling beams
items.text: Room length and width, ceiling height, which way the joists run, and how many beams you're picturing.

items.title: Shutters
items.text: Height and width of every window opening. Measure each one, even if they look identical.

items.title: Mantels and corbels
items.text: Width and height of the wall or fireplace, and what the piece will hold. Check the specs before anything rests on it.

items.title: Moulding and trim
items.text: Length of each wall, ceiling height, and a count of inside and outside corners.

items.title: Columns
items.text: Floor-to-ceiling height, and whether it's decorative or needs to carry weight. The specs will tell you.

blocks.title: Get a second set of eyes

items.title: Sketch it
items.text: A rough drawing with dimensions is plenty.

items.title: Take two photos
items.text: One wide shot of the space, one close-up of where it mounts.

items.title: Send or call
items.text: Email cs@architecturaldepot.com or call 1-888-573-3768 and we'll walk through sizes with you.

steps.ps: Phones are answered Mon-Fri 8am-6pm CT and Sat 8am-12pm CT.
